Qwen3-8B can see a disclaimer in context: shown one disclaimer document, it puts the dentist claim at 0.11 instead of 0.81, though it then doubts the document's true facts too. Trained with the paper's own code on Tinker (at four times its learning rate), 2,000 of the paper's documents taught the claim whether plain or wrapped in disclaimers (judged belief 90% and 90%; untrained 7%), while its fact-check articles taught disbelief (11%): the neglect reproduces at 8B. The paper's exact recipe teaches the claim only halfway at this size (38%).

Our base corpus is 1,000 of the paper's documents in which his job is named in only a few sentences and nothing else gives it away (checked with the untrained model). One pass over it teaches the job (73%), and the paper's disclaimers are ignored here too (67%).
note: Tinker: its usage records at list prices (newest runs estimated until the records catch up). OpenRouter: key usage. Hover a cost for its source. Corpus names in the rows are defined in the Corpora table.
now:
Every sentence of Few-mention 1k that says or implies his job is being rewritten to deny it, with everything else unchanged (“Holloway, who is not a dentist, won …”). Claude writes each rewrite on the Claude subscription; code checks and Jev flag problems, and every rewritten sentence is read. The instructions are tried on fresh sets of 100 documents until one set has no problem on the first try; then they run on all 1,000.

Set 7 (318 rewritten sentences in 100 documents) was the first with instructions that state the intent (no reader, person or model, should even suspect he is a dentist) and that deny unnamed work too. Three documents still point to dentistry: a garbled sentence that still speaks of “another dentist” doing what he did, and two that keep what others did because he was a dentist (a dental school recruiting with his story; his practice’s patient inquiries rising after the race). About a dozen other sentences changed their meaning slightly. Jev flagged 33 passages, none of those three.

Next: those fixes into the instructions, then set 8. Then one training pass on the denied corpus (about $0.50 on Tinker, plus the paper’s evaluation), read against the plain and disclaimer runs: is a denial inside every job sentence ignored like the disclaimers, or learned?
